newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money down slightly at 3.05 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money down slightly at 3.05 pct.

text.p: German call money rates eased slightly on Wednesday to 3.05 percent from 3.05/3.10 percent after the Bundesbank injected a net 2.1 billion marks into the market in its weekly tender.
Dealers said rates could ease further to 3.00/05 percent as the weekend approached, but said demand would likely remain strong as reserve deposits with the central bank remained below requirements.
The Bundesbank allocated 69.9 billion marks in repo funds, for a slightly higher fund injection than general market expectations for additional funds of up to two billion marks.

Bank deposits with the Bundesbank were 37.6 billion marks on Tuesday, up from 36.7 billion and the monthly average was unchanged at 37.2 billion marks. Borrowings at the Lombard window were negligible.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was at 3.07650 on Wednesday versus 3.10867.
